# Parametric PDEs: basis or conditioning? {#sec-parametric}

The learned-BIE studies of @sec-learned-bie fixed the PDE and varied
geometry, drive, and boundary condition. This chapter varies the *operator
itself*: the screened Laplace (modified Helmholtz) equation

$$
\Delta u - \kappa^2 u = 0 \ \text{ in } \Omega,
\qquad u = g \ \text{ on } \Gamma,
$$

with the dimensionless screening group $\tilde\kappa = \kappa L$ supplied in
`global_data`. This is the smallest testbed for a question that decides the
architecture of any parametric surrogate:

> Should a global PDE parameter enter through the **kernel basis** (the
> parameter-dependent fundamental solutions), or through **learned
> coefficient conditioning** (a network mapping $\tilde\kappa$ to
> coefficients of a fixed basis)?

The second option is exactly the role a learned boundary *encoder* would play
in the `MeshTransformer` marriage: conditioning decoder coefficients on
global operator data. Whether that pattern extrapolates is therefore the real
question.

## Setup

The testbed (`screened_laplace.py`) is self-contained: randomized disks
(radius, center, phase), exact Bessel-series Dirichlet solutions
$I_m(\kappa r)/I_m(\kappa R)\,e^{im\theta}$, and the reference length equal
to the radius so `screening` is exactly $\tilde\kappa$. Four models share the
identical drive-linear Richardson solve ($\tilde T = \tfrac12 I + \tilde K$,
zero-kernel init in the convergent regime — the Neumann gauge lesson of
@sec-neumann applied),
exact linearity in the boundary data, O(2)/similarity invariance, and
query-set independence. There is no constant lift: constants do not solve
the screened equation. They differ only in where $\tilde\kappa$ enters:

| model | params | basis | $\tilde\kappa$ enters via |
|---|--:|---|---|
| `yukawa` | 10 | $K_0(\tilde\kappa\rho)$, $\tilde\kappa K_1(\tilde\kappa\rho)\frac{n\cdot r}{\rho}$ | the basis (analytically) |
| `conditioned_yukawa` | 1,194 | same Yukawa basis | basis **and** MLP $\tilde\kappa \mapsto$ coefficients |
| `conditioned_harmonic` | 1,293 | fixed Laplace harmonic basis @eq-laurent | MLP conditioning only |
| `conditioned_union` | 1,359 | Yukawa $\cup$ harmonic | MLP conditioning over the union |

: The four arms. Training: $\tilde\kappa \in [0.5, 2]$, modes $\{0..3\}$, 2,000 steps, seed 17. Evaluation: OOD-high $\tilde\kappa \in [3,5]$, OOD-low $\tilde\kappa \in [0.05, 0.3]$, unseen modes $\{4,5,6\}$. {#tbl-arms}

The Yukawa kernels have no elementary panel antiderivative, so panels use
16-node Gauss–Legendre quadrature. The original experiment zeroed the complete
self-panel entry. That is not a benign fixed-resolution knob: the omitted
$K_0$ single-layer contribution scales as
$h[-\log(\tilde\kappa h)+O(1)]$ and therefore grows toward the low-screening
limit. One infrastructure note with reuse value:
`torch.special.modified_bessel_k0/k1` lack autograd derivatives, so the
testbed adds custom `Function`s with the analytic recurrences
$K_0' = -K_1$, $K_1' = -K_0 - K_1/z$, tested through nested derivatives.

::: {.callout-warning title="EDIT: the specialist density solve is not yet a valid BIE control"}
The density iteration fixes the trace jump at $+\tfrac12 I$ while learning the
coefficient $c_d$ of a double-layer kernel. **A subsequent orientation audit
corrected the sign in the first version of this warning:** the stored
counter-clockwise panels receive inward line normals from `Mesh`, so the
implemented interior jump is $+\pi c_d I$. It agrees with the fixed jump only
at $c_d=+1/(2\pi)$, which was not enforced. The earlier
$-\pi c_d$ statement implicitly assumed outward normals.
Zeroing the single-layer diagonal creates a second, screening-dependent trace
error. The field-error numbers below remain measurements of the executed
models, and their interior PDE residual is still structural, but claims about
a correct boundary trace or the mechanism of low-screening failure are
withdrawn pending a corrected no-learning test.
:::

## Results

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Relative L2 by evaluation split for the four arms (seed 17, 2,000
#|   steps; checked-in learned_bie_2026-07-02.json, iteration 3). Log scale:
#|   the low-screening split spans four orders of magnitude. Values above
#|   each bar. The 10-parameter physics-in-basis model wins high-screening
#|   OOD; only the (wrong-basis) harmonic conditioner remains accurate as kappa -> 0
#|   limit, because harmonic IS that limit.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

results = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "learned_bie_2026-07-02.json"))
arms = results["iteration_3_parametric_conditioning"]["results_seed17_2000steps"]

order = ["yukawa_10p", "conditioned_yukawa", "conditioned_harmonic", "conditioned_union"]
labels = ["yukawa\n(10 p, basis)", "conditioned\nyukawa (1,194 p)",
          "conditioned\nharmonic (1,293 p)", "conditioned\nunion (1,359 p)"]
colors = ["#2a78d6", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#4a3aa7"]
splits = [("id", "ID"), ("ood_high", "OOD high $\\tilde\\kappa\\in[3,5]$"),
          ("ood_low", "OOD low $\\tilde\\kappa\\in[0.05,0.3]$"),
          ("unseen_modes", "unseen modes {4,5,6}")]

x = np.arange(len(splits))
width = 0.2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 3.8))
for i, (arm, label, color) in enumerate(zip(order, labels, colors)):
    values = [arms[arm][key] for key, _ in splits]
    bars = ax.bar(x + (i - 1.5) * width, values, width * 0.92, color=color,
                  label=label.replace("\n", " "))
    for bar, value in zip(bars, values):
        text = f"{value:.4f}" if value < 0.01 else f"{value:.3g}"
        ax.annotate(text, (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, value),
                    textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 2), ha="center",
                    fontsize=6.8, color="#52514e", rotation=90, va="bottom")
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_ylim(2e-4, 3e2)
ax.set_xticks(x, [name for _, name in splits], fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel(r"relative $L^2$ (log scale)")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="upper left")
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

| model | params | ID | OOD-high | OOD-low | unseen modes | PDE residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| yukawa (basis) | 10 | 0.0033 | **0.0158** | 8.68 | 0.0080 | **0.0** |
| conditioned yukawa | 1,194 | **0.0005** | 0.0474 | 28.0 | 0.0060 | 0.0 |
| conditioned harmonic | 1,293 | 0.0613 | 0.3101 | **0.0035** | 0.0459 | 1.646 |
| conditioned union | 1,359 | 0.0020 | 0.0663 | 25.0 | 0.0073 | 0.14 |

: The four-arm results (checked-in key `iteration_3_parametric_conditioning`). The harmonic arm's PDE residual $1.646 = \mathbb E[\tilde\kappa^2]$ over the training range — it measures precisely the operator mismatch $\|(\Delta - \kappa^2)u\|$ of a basis that satisfies the wrong PDE. {#tbl-screened}

::: {.callout-important title="EDIT: the corrected canonical control reverses the low-screening conclusion"}
A parameter-free replication fixed the double-layer coefficient at
$c_d=1/(2\pi)$ in the implementation's inward-normal convention, retained
the matching $+\tfrac12 I$ jump, removed the unstable single-layer charge
mode, and used the complete trace. On 64 fresh cases per split, the dense and
eight-step controls scored:

| corrected control | ID | OOD-high | OOD-low | unseen modes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dense canonical double layer | 0.00110 | 0.00349 | 0.000602 | 0.00467 |
| eight shared residual steps | 0.000974 | 0.00281 | 0.000928 | 0.00628 |

The old 8.7--28 low-screening detonation is therefore **not inherent to
placing $\tilde\kappa$ in a Yukawa kernel**. A separate manufactured test
identified two independent failures in the old single-layer path:
charge-mode Richardson instability and a deleted self panel. The archived
coefficients are unavailable, so their individual shares of the historical
error remain unknown. Data:
[corrected full-bank control](../results/screened_canonical_double_layer_2026-07-29_job5689394/artifacts/report.json)
and [mechanism discriminator](../results/screened_trace_mechanism_2026-07-29/report.json).
:::

## Findings

1. **Correct analytic structure is decisive.** The canonical double layer
   satisfies the screened operator in the interior and remains below 0.0063
   field error on every tested parameter and mode split without learned
   coefficients.
2. **The historical low-screening failure was an instrument failure, not a
   kernel-family limit.** Its single-layer charge mode becomes
   Richardson-unstable as $\tilde\kappa\to0$, while deleting the self panel
   independently creates 22--53% error even for a zero-charge density.
3. **Coefficient conditioning has not earned its place on disks.** The old
   conditioned Yukawa arm improved interpolation inside a trace-inconsistent
   model, then failed both screening extrapolations. The corrected fixed
   coefficient is accurate in all four regimes.
4. **Solver tolerance still matters.** Eight shared residual steps track the
   dense field within 0.0021 on every case, but their $10^{-3}$ truncation
   floor eventually masks boundary refinement. This identifies iteration
   accuracy, not parameter conditioning, as the next controlled variable.

## The design rule

> **Disk-family result:** known operator dependence belongs in a correctly
> normalized fundamental-solution kernel; the trace jump and singular
> coefficient must be coupled analytically, and solver accuracy should be
> controlled by a residual rather than a fixed iteration count.

Read against @sec-mesh-attention, this fixes the division of labor for the
`MeshTransformer` marriage: the *decoder* should be a kernel basis carrying
all operator dependence analytically (PDE-conforming where the operator is
known — which, under the product scope, it is not); the *encoder*'s
evidence-backed role is conditioning coefficients on geometry and operator
data **within** the training distribution. The screened experiment does not
establish a general extrapolation law for learned conditioning.

Caveats: the corrected result is parameter-free and uses 64 cases per split,
but still covers disks only. The geometry analogue—whether the same
residual-controlled trace solver remains effective on deformed boundaries—is the next
required test (@sec-future).

## Under the product scope

The design rule assumes the operator's fundamental solutions are available
to place in the basis. Under the problem statement in the front matter they
are not — for the real targets the operator itself is not perfectly
knowable. The experiment therefore supports a narrower limitation:
coefficient conditioning cannot be assumed to extrapolate beyond its
operator-parameter training range. Parameter and spectral extrapolation must
not be promised in the unknown-PDE setting; what can be tested is
in-distribution fidelity plus whatever transfer a learned
singularity-dictionary prior (@sec-future) provides on held-out axes. The
study's value under this scope is
diagnostic: a correct known-PDE double layer is accurate throughout the
screening range, while the harmonic-biased generalist remains a fallback when
the operator is unknown but gives up both accuracy and operator fidelity. The full
architecture — $\tilde\kappa$ conditioning through the `MeshTransformer`
operator encoder over a harmonic-biased kernel dictionary — is evaluated
directly in @sec-screened.
